title: Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery — Cost-of-Collection Deductions by Recent Offset Activity
content:
VA's cost of collecting a debt in **Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery** sets the cost deduction taken off the recovery when a compromise offer is measured.

**Rule.** When a benefit offset posted on the debt in each of the last three calendar months counted back from today (three or more offsets in that period), the offset-collection cost of 2 percent is deducted. When no offset posted on the debt in that period, the billing cost of 10 percent is deducted. With one or two offsets in that period, this rule sets no cost deduction.

The deduction is taken off the recovery as a percentage of the recovery. A benefit offset is an amount withheld from a VA benefit payment and applied to the debt; direct payments do not count. A period of so many calendar months counted back from today covers the dates from which fewer than that many whole calendar months have passed to today: on 20 October, the last six months include 21 April but not 20 April.

| Benefit offsets posted in the last three calendar months | Cost deduction |
|---|---|
| 3 or more | 2 percent of the recovery |
| None | 10 percent of the recovery |
| 1 or 2 | Not set by this rule |

**Hypothetical cases.** A recovery of 5,000.00 USD on a debt offset every month: 100.00 USD deducted, leaving 4,900.00 USD. The same recovery on a debt with no offsets in the period: 500.00 USD deducted, leaving 4,500.00 USD.
